Disorders located in the sclera; an immune mechanism is not universal across this umbrella.
Benign neoplasm arising in breast tissue, which has no axis.
Lysosomal glycoprotein storage disorder. Splenomegaly and gout lack frequencies sufficient to establish common direct organ damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 23/23 patients.
Defining renal phosphate wasting, hypophosphatemia and rickets. Dentin defects/odontodysplasia occur in 30-79%; nephrocalcinosis is often treatment-related.
Defining intestinal hypoperistalsis and microcolon with dysfunctional enlarged urinary bladder; visceral smooth muscle disease.
Defining myofibrillar muscle degeneration and axonal motor neuropathy. Isolated hearing, bladder and respiratory reports do not establish population frequency >=30%.
Suppurative intraocular infection, usually bacterial and occasionally fungal.
Defined by retinal malignancy together with an intracranial pineal or suprasellar neuroectodermal tumor.
Vitamin B6 deficiency with anemia. Neuropathy, dermatitis and oral inflammation are possible, but common persistent involvement is not established.
Reduced bone strength and fragility fractures in premenopausal women; no specific endocrine disease is intrinsic to this concept.
CRYBB3-related nonsyndromic lens cataract; no extraocular disease is defined.
Neonatal bacterial bloodstream infection; bloodstream location alone does not establish disease of blood cells, marrow or coagulation.
Cutaneous ectoparasitic infestation, including scabies and trombiculiasis.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction. Ophthalmoplegia and muscle weakness reflect junction dysfunction rather than separate eye or muscle disease.
Defining subcutaneous fat loss and insulin resistance; hepatic lipid deposition in 80-99%; muscle atrophy in 3/3 and myopathy in 1/3. Hypertension is separately coded.
Aldosterone synthesis deficiency causing hyperkalemia, hyponatremia and salt wasting; no intrinsic renal tissue disease is established.
Disease located in the parathyroid glands; downstream organ effects vary across the umbrella.
Defective distal tubular electrolyte transport defines renal dysfunction with hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease with proximal weakness and minicore lesions; no common independent damage to another axis is established.
Infantile focal epilepsy; development is normal and ictal apnea does not establish pulmonary disease.
Polyomavirus infection umbrella; renal/urinary disease and CNS disease depend on viral species and host context, without established >=30% involvement across the group.
Inherited dilated cardiomyopathy defined by myocardial disease.
